conviction_note: Event and 07:00 bmo timing confirmed from the issuer's own calendar and RNS record. The half is only partly pre-released: the 30 June AGM update gave direction but no profit figure, so the move sits in the H1 underlying PBT number and in whether the FY26/27 outlook (still qualitative) gets firmed or raised. Saga has raised its outlook at each of its last three scheduled releases, fuel and FX are 100% hedged for FY27, and Carnival's record deposits and raised guide on 09-29 point the same way, so the tilt is positive. Two things hold p_up near 57: the bar has only one source (Berenberg's +24% FY27 PBT), and the stock jumped about 5% at 10:30 BST on 09-29 on no RNS and no news I could find, which raises the entry price. abs 7.5 x (2x0.57-1) = 1.05, and the findings sum to 1.1.

already_public.what: AGM trading update covering 1 Feb-29 Jun 2026: group trading in line with expectations and on track for FY guidance; Cruise ahead of expectations; Ocean H1 revenue ahead (booked per diems +13%, load factor 93%); River H1 revenue up (per diems +4%, load 93%); Holidays H1 revenue and passengers ahead but FY passengers possibly slightly behind on the Middle East; Insurance Broking in line; £10.5m Ageas contingent consideration triggered; Net Debt £464.7m at 31 May, leverage 3.2x; commodity and FX fully hedged to end-2027

FY26/27 outlook (qualitative only): Underlying PBT to 'take a further step forward'; Travel UPBT to grow; Insurance Broking UPBT at least in line with 2025/26; Net Debt and leverage to fall further; 100% FX hedged for 26/27 and 27/28, 100%/75% oil hedged; medium-term target of at least £100m UPBT and leverage below 2.0x by Jan 2030
Interim results date: 30 September 2026, stated in the AGM RNS and on the issuer's financial calendar

new_in_release.expect: H1 underlying PBT (prior year H1 £23.5m). Expected above prior year and modestly above the bar: Ocean per diems +13% on a hedged cost base, lower net debt so lower finance costs. Up.

The FY26/27 outlook is qualitative ('further step forward'). The release may firm it to 'ahead of' or quantify it, which is what Saga did at the Sept-2025 interims, the Jan-2026 trading update and the Apr-2026 prelims. I lean up on this line, and it is the line that decides the size of the move.
Cruise forward bookings into FY27/28 (Carnival reported record 2027 booked occupancy on 09-29) and Holidays short-haul mix after the Middle East. Mixed, leaning up.
Net debt at 31 July against £464.7m at 31 May, and the £49.1m Ageas working-capital unwind, which is excluded from Net Debt but sits inside Available Cash. Unknown. This is the Luceco-type risk.
Unlikely to be reinstated with leverage at 3.2x and a <2.0x target by 2030. No change expected.
Timing of the Ageas renewals transition and the insurance H2 profile. Unknown.

bar: Unsourced to two agreeing estimates. The bar I used is the company's own qualitative FY26/27 guide of a 'further step forward' in Underlying PBT from £44.2m (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/saga--saga/preliminary-results-for-the-year-ended-31-jan-2026/9520320), plus one broker: Berenberg's 24% FY27 PBT growth, which implies about £55m (https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/berenberg-bullish-on-saga-as-cruise-demand-and-deleveraging-drive-growth-4783025, 2026-07-09). No H1 consensus found. Sizes are capped accordingly.
session_check: bmo. Every scheduled Saga results release in the RNS record was at 07:00 London: interims 24 Sep 2025 07:00, trading update 29 Jan 2026 07:00, prelims 15 Apr 2026 07:00, AGM update 30 Jun 2026 07:00 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/SAGA). The issuer's calendar lists 'Wednesday 30 September 2026 Interim results' (https://corporate.saga.co.uk/investors/financial-calendar/), and the 30 Jun RNS says the interims 'will be announced on 30 September 2026'. The time of day is inferred from the 07:00 pattern because no Notice of Results RNS was issued.
positioning_check: FCA aggregated net short 2.72% (position date 2026-09-16, file read 2026-09-29, https://www.fca.org.uk/publication/documents/aggregated-current-net-short-positions.csv), up from 2.32%, so building +0.40pp into the print. The individual holders are no longer public: the FCA per-holder file is now 'Historic Disclosures 10.07.2026', and Investegate shows only Systematica at 0.5% as active (07-Jul-2026). At about 146m shares and roughly 450k shares a day, 2.72% is about 9 days of volume, which is meaningful fuel on a name whose last 8 results or trading-update reactions were all positive. On the other side, JPMorgan Asset Management raised its long from 5.46% to 5.75% (TR-1 07-Sep-2026, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/saga--saga/holding-s-in-company/9759203).

findings.finding: Saga has now beaten or raised at three consecutive scheduled releases, and the 30 Jun update already said Cruise was 'performing ahead of expectations' while the group guide stayed qualitative. The open question for this release is whether the FY26/27 outlook gets firmed or raised. Carnival, the largest direct peer, reported on 09-29 (09:15 ET, after the 10:30 BST Saga jump) record deposits, record 2027 booked occupancy and pricing, and a raised FY guide despite higher fuel.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sept-2025 interims raised FY UPBT to 'in line with prior year' from lower: +6.68% on the day (and +5.4% and +8.8% on the next two sessions per the Yahoo tape). Jan-2026 trading update raised: +15.21%. Apr-2026 prelims 'ahead of guidance': +6.01%. Jun-2026 AGM 'in line': +6.66% close after a -10% intraday low.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide is still qualitative, so there is no number for the market to have priced. The stock fell from 738p (7 Aug) to 590p (15 Sep), about -20%, into the print, which is not how a name positioned for an upgrade trades, and disclosed shorts built from 2.32% to 2.72%. It is partly priced: the stock rose about 5% on 09-29 at 10:30 BST with no RNS, so some anticipation is already in the entry price. That is why this is +0.8 and not larger.
findings.independence: Carnival Q3 FY26 release, a different company and a different document: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carnival-corporation-outperforms-guidance-delivering-best-ever-revenues-net-yields-and-net-income-302892070.html (2026-09-29 09:15 ET). Also the Sept-2025 interim RNS showing the same pattern of raising at interims: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/saga--saga/2025-26-interim-results-statement-replacement/9128374

findings.finding: Saga is 100% hedged on fuel for FY26/27 (75% for 27/28) and fully hedged on FX, yet it fell with the cruise sector as oil rose in September (-3.8% on 9 Sep, the day NCLH slid on oil). If the interims restate that a fuel spike does not reach FY27 profit, the part of that drawdown caused by oil should reverse.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior release where fuel was the surprise line. The Jun-2026 AGM update, which carried the 'fully hedged to end of 2027' sentence, closed +6.66%.
findings.why_not_priced: The hedge is public, but the September tape moved Saga with unhedged US cruise lines on oil days, which would not happen if the hedge were fully reflected. This rests on inference: the drawdown's cause is not established in any Saga document. That is why the size is small, and why today's recovery may already have taken part of it.
findings.independence: The cruise sector sold off on oil on 2026-09-09: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/09/norwegian-slides-3-as-rising-oil-undercuts-fuel-cost-relief-hopes-carnival-and-royal-caribbean-trail/ (a sector proxy, not a Saga document)

outside_window.finding: Medium-term target of at least £100m UPBT and leverage below 2.0x by January 2030. Any re-affirmation is real but not resolvable in the window beyond what the guidance finding already carries.

baseline_tension: The findings agree with the positive priced lean (+0.86, dominated by short_squeeze) but go against the 5-day run-up (+4.8%, most of it from the unexplained 09-29 jump). So p_up is held at 57 rather than the ~62 the track record alone would suggest, and the emitted number stays at the findings' sum rather than above it.
language_note: The UK local half is source locality, not language. The RNS record via Investegate is what confirmed the date, the 07:00 timing pattern and the TR-1 showing JPMorgan AM building to 5.75%. The FCA aggregate showed shorts building to 2.72%. The domestic UK insurance trade press (Insurance Business, Insurance Age) and Travel Weekly UK added nothing the RNS had not already said. Beyond the RNS itself, nothing the English wire sources did not already carry.
lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the AGM update had already said Cruise was ahead of expectations, so the guidance finding is framed only on what is not yet public (a firmed or raised FY outlook), not on H1 Cruise strength. Its size stayed +0.8.

'A narrow proxy loses... macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': the fuel-hedge finding rests on attributing the September drawdown to oil from a sector co-move, so it was cut from +0.4 to +0.3.

'Too small about the move' plus 'the move is in the guide': abs_move_pct raised from 7.0 to 7.5, because a guidance change is plausible (about 9% median when one happens) on a 3-7-analyst name with a building short. p_up trimmed 58 to 57 because there is no sourced, not-yet-public number.
'Cash can outweigh a raised guide': added the £49.1m Ageas working-capital unwind and net debt at 31 July as an explicit cash_flow line in new_in_release. No size change.
